_about: Initial import only. Once loaded, places live in the D1 database and are edited from the site. Coordinates, photos and credits come from Wikidata, Wikimedia Commons and OpenStreetMap (ODbL). Opening hours are a starting point and must be checked (hours_verified = 0).

places.name: Galerie Vivienne
places.summary: The most elegant of the passages: mosaic floors, a glass roof and an old bookshop.
places.hours_note: Open daily, roughly 8:30 to 20:30.
places.photo: P1040471 Paris II galerie Vivienne rwk.JPG

places.name: Galerie Colbert
places.summary: Vivienne's quiet neighbour, with a beautiful glass rotunda.

places.name: Passage des Panoramas
places.summary: One of the oldest covered passages, full of stamp dealers and little restaurants.

places.name: Passage Jouffroy
places.summary: Toy shops, a doll hospital and the back door of the Musée Grévin.
places.photo: P1020618 Paris IX Passage Jouffroy rwk.JPG

places.name: Passage Verdeau
places.summary: Old photos, prints and antique shops, in the continuation of Jouffroy.

places.name: Galerie Véro-Dodat
places.summary: Black and white floor, dark wood shopfronts: the most theatrical passage.

places.name: Passage du Grand-Cerf
places.summary: The tallest glass roof of all the passages, with designers' workshops.

places.name: Passage Choiseul
places.summary: A long, lively passage near the Opéra, home of the Bouffes-Parisiens theatre.

places.name: Passage des Princes
places.summary: The last passage to be built, now full of toys and model trains.

places.name: Passage du Caire
places.summary: The longest passage, with Egyptian-style faces on its façade.

places.name: Passage Brady
places.summary: Little India: spices, sarees and some of the best curries in Paris.

places.name: Passage Molière
places.summary: A tiny, quiet passage next to the Théâtre Molière, now a poetry house.

places.name: Musée de Montmartre
places.summary: Renoir's gardens, Suzanne Valadon's studio and a view over the vineyard.
places.hours_note: Until 19:00 from April to September.
places.photo: Musée de Montmartre - maison du Bel Air.jpg

places.name: Musée de la Vie romantique
places.summary: A green-shuttered house at the end of a cobbled lane, with a tea room in the garden.

places.name: Musée du Louvre
places.summary: The biggest museum in the world. Pick two or three rooms rather than everything.
places.hours_note: Closed on Tuesdays. Book a time slot online.

places.name: Musée Jacquemart-André
places.summary: A sumptuous 19th-century mansion, and one of the prettiest cafés in Paris.

places.name: Musée Nissim de Camondo
places.summary: A collector's home frozen in the 1930s, down to the kitchens.

places.name: Musée Gustave Moreau
places.summary: The painter's studio, walls covered in paintings, and a famous spiral staircase.

places.name: Maison de Victor Hugo
places.summary: Victor Hugo's flat on the Place des Vosges, with his astonishing Chinese room.
places.photo: PARIS Place des Vosges, Maison de Victor Hugo 2.jpg

places.name: Musée Eugène-Delacroix
places.summary: Delacroix's last studio, hidden behind a small secret garden.

places.name: Musée Cognacq-Jay
places.summary: 18th-century art in a Marais mansion, calm and rarely crowded.

places.name: Musée Zadkine
places.summary: A sculptor's house and garden, two minutes from the Luxembourg.

places.name: Musée Marmottan Monet
places.summary: The world's largest Monet collection, including Impression, Sunrise.

places.name: Musée d'Orsay
places.summary: Impressionists in a former railway station. Don't miss the clock window.

places.name: Musée de l'Orangerie
places.summary: Monet's Water Lilies in two oval rooms lit by daylight.

places.name: Musée Rodin
places.summary: The Thinker in a rose garden, and a mansion full of marble.
places.photo: L'hôtel Biron (musée Rodin) à Paris, 13 juin 2021 01.jpg

places.name: Petit Palais
places.summary: A golden palace with a hidden garden courtyard and café.
places.hours_note: Late opening on some evenings for exhibitions.

places.name: Musée Carnavalet
places.summary: The history of Paris, from old shop signs to Proust's bedroom.

places.name: Musée de Cluny
places.summary: Medieval treasures and The Lady and the Unicorn tapestries.

places.name: Musée des Arts forains
places.summary: Old fairground rides you can actually ride, in Bercy's wine warehouses.
places.hours_note: Guided visits on booking only.

places.name: Musée de la Chasse et de la Nature
places.summary: A cabinet of curiosities mixing stuffed animals and contemporary art.
places.photo: P1000961 Paris III Rue des Archives Musée de la chasse reductwk.JPG

places.name: Bourse de Commerce
places.summary: Contemporary art under a painted dome, redesigned by Tadao Ando.

places.name: Sainte-Chapelle
places.summary: Walls made of stained glass. Go on a sunny day.
places.hours_note: Until 19:00 from April to September.

places.name: Palais Garnier
places.summary: The opera house of The Phantom of the Opera: gold, marble and a Chagall ceiling.
places.hours_note: Visits can close for rehearsals and matinées.
places.photo: Paris Opera full frontal architecture, May 2009.jpg

places.name: Castel Béranger
places.summary: Hector Guimard's Art Nouveau masterpiece. Look at the entrance gate.
places.hours_note: Private flats: façade only.

places.name: Immeuble Lavirotte
places.summary: The wildest Art Nouveau door in Paris, a short walk from the Eiffel Tower.
places.hours_note: Private flats: façade only.

places.name: Grande Mosquée de Paris
places.summary: Moorish courtyards and gardens, and mint tea on the terrace next door.
places.hours_note: Closed to visitors on Fridays.

places.name: Hôtel de Sully
places.summary: A Renaissance courtyard and garden, and a secret shortcut to the Place des Vosges.
places.hours_note: Courtyard and garden open during the day.

places.name: Bibliothèque Sainte-Geneviève
places.summary: A breathtaking iron-vaulted reading room, opposite the Panthéon.
places.hours_note: Reading room on access card; check visit conditions.
places.photo: Salle de lecture Bibliotheque Sainte-Genevieve n11.jpg

places.name: La Samaritaine
places.summary: An Art Nouveau department store with a peacock fresco under its glass roof.
places.photo: La Samaritaine and Statue of Henri IV.jpg

places.name: Hôtel de Ville
places.summary: The city hall, a neo-Renaissance wedding cake with free exhibitions.

places.name: Galeries Lafayette rooftop
places.summary: A free rooftop terrace on top of the department store, facing the Opéra Garnier, with Paris all around. Don't miss the stained-glass dome inside on the way up.
places.tip: Free. Lovely by day or at night.
places.hours_note: Open with the store: check the closing time before going at night.
places.photo: Opéra Garnier vu de la terrasse des Galeries Lafayette.jpg

places.name: Rue Crémieux
places.summary: Pastel houses and painted shutters. Residents ask for quiet: no posing on doorsteps.

places.name: Rue de l'Abreuvoir
places.summary: The Montmartre postcard: the pink house, cobbles and a view of the Sacré-Cœur.

places.name: Rue Saint-Rustique
places.summary: One of the oldest streets in Montmartre, narrow and still cobbled.

places.name: Rue des Thermopyles
places.summary: A village lane in the 14th, under wisteria and climbing plants.

places.name: Rue Berton
places.summary: A countryside lane behind Balzac's house, with gas lamps and old walls.

places.name: Cour du Commerce-Saint-André
places.summary: A cobbled passage with Le Procope, the oldest café in Paris.
places.photo: P1020083 Paris VI Cour du Commerce-Saint-André reductwk.JPG

places.name: Rue de Furstemberg
places.summary: A tiny square with paulownia trees and a five-globe lamp, beside Delacroix's studio.

places.name: Cité florale
places.summary: Little houses on streets named after flowers: Wisteria, Iris, Orchids...

places.name: Place Dauphine
places.summary: A secret triangle on the Île de la Cité, with chestnut trees and pétanque.

places.name: Place des Vosges
places.summary: The oldest planned square in Paris: red brick arcades and lawns to sit on.

places.name: Jardin du Palais-Royal
places.summary: Lime tree alleys, arcades and the striped Buren columns.
places.hours_note: Until 22:30 in summer.

places.name: Square du Vert-Galant
places.summary: The tip of the Île de la Cité, at water level. Picnic at sunset.

places.name: Dancing on the Seine (Quai Saint-Bernard)
places.address: Jardin Tino-Rossi, quai Saint-Bernard, 5th — across the river from Gare de Lyon
places.summary: On warm evenings, the little stone amphitheatres by the river fill with people dancing tango, salsa, rock and swing. Anyone can join or just watch.
places.tip: Go in the evening, after dinner.
places.hours_note: Mostly on fine evenings in the warmer months.

places.name: Place des Abbesses
places.summary: Street musicians play by the Art Nouveau metro entrance and the carousel, a lively stop on the way up to Montmartre.

places.name: Home — Bois-Colombes station
places.summary: Where the day starts and ends. Direct trains to Paris Saint-Lazare.

places.name: Seine cruise on a Bateau-Mouche
places.summary: The classic boat ride past Notre-Dame, the Louvre and the Eiffel Tower, leaving from the Pont de l'Alma.
places.hours_note: In winter, departures run from mid-morning until about 21:30.

places.name: Palace of Versailles
places.summary: The Hall of Mirrors, the royal apartments and huge gardens. Take the RER C to Versailles Château Rive Gauche.
places.hours_note: Closed on Mondays.
places.photo: Vue aérienne du domaine de Versailles par ToucanWings - Creative Commons By Sa 3.0 - 083.jpg

places.name: Eiffel Tower
places.summary: Go up for the view, or just watch it sparkle for five minutes at the start of every hour after dark.

places.name: Arc de Triomphe rooftop
places.summary: Climb the stairs to the terrace and watch the twelve avenues fan out from the Étoile.

places.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
places.summary: The cathedral reopened after the fire, its stone and windows bright again. Point Zero of French roads is on the square.

places.name: Sacré-Cœur and its dome
places.summary: The white basilica on top of Montmartre. Climb the dome for one of the highest views over Paris.

places.name: Catacombs of Paris
places.summary: Old quarry tunnels lined with the bones of millions of Parisians. Strange, quiet and unforgettable.
places.hours_note: Book a time slot online: tickets sell out.

places.name: Père-Lachaise cemetery
places.summary: A romantic hillside of tombs and trees: Oscar Wilde, Édith Piaf, Chopin, Jim Morrison. Beautiful in autumn.
places.photo: Main gate of the Père-Lachaise Cemetery, Paris 13 June 2014.jpg

places.name: Paris Sewer Museum
places.summary: Walk through real sewer galleries under the Quai d'Orsay and learn how the city works underground.

places.name: Deyrolle
places.summary: A cabinet-of-curiosities shop on rue du Bac: stuffed lions, butterflies and old school charts.

places.name: Studio 28 cinema
places.summary: A tiny historic cinema in Montmartre, open since 1928, with a little garden bar.

places.name: Swim at the Piscine des Amiraux
places.summary: A 1920s Art Deco public pool with two floors of changing cabins, seen in Amélie.
places.hours_note: Bring a swimsuit.
places.photo: Immeuble Sauvage - piscine des amiraux - rue des amiraux 2.JPG

places.name: Le Train Bleu
places.summary: A Belle Époque dining room inside the Gare de Lyon, all gold and painted ceilings. Or just a drink at the bar.
places.hours_note: Book ahead for a table.

places.name: Coulée verte René-Dumont
places.summary: A garden walk on an old railway viaduct, starting near Bastille and heading east above the streets.

places.name: Canal Saint-Martin
places.summary: Iron footbridges, locks and plane trees. Walk along the water, then stop in one of the cafés.

places.name: Marché des Enfants Rouges
places.summary: The oldest covered market in Paris, in the Marais: Moroccan, Japanese and Italian stalls for lunch.
places.hours_note: Closed on Mondays.

places.name: Saint-Ouen flea market
places.summary: A maze of antique dealers, vintage clothes and odd objects just north of Paris.
places.hours_note: Open from Saturday to Monday.

places.name: Shakespeare and Company
places.summary: The famous English bookshop facing Notre-Dame, with a reading room upstairs and a café next door.

places.name: Atelier des Lumières
places.summary: Immersive digital art shows projected on every wall of a former foundry.

places.name: Jardin des Plantes
places.summary: Botanical gardens, glasshouses and the Grande Galerie de l'Évolution. From mid-November, the Festival of Lights fills it at night.
places.best_time: Afternoon, or evening for the lights

places.name: Tuileries Garden
places.summary: The royal garden between the Louvre and Concorde. In November its Christmas market opens with a big wheel.
places.photo: Grande Roue de Paris - Louvre et Jardins des Tuileries.jpg

places.name: Jardin du Luxembourg
places.summary: Green chairs, the Medici fountain and the Senate palace: the Parisians' favourite garden.

places.name: Montparnasse Tower viewpoint
places.summary: A rooftop view over all of Paris, with the Eiffel Tower in the picture.
places.photo: Remote view of the Tour Montparnasse & Eiffel Tower in 2005.jpg

places.name: Château de Fontainebleau
places.summary: Eight centuries of kings in one palace, then a walk in the forest. Trains leave from the Gare de Lyon.
places.photo: Le Grand Escalier à Fer de Cheval.jpg

places.name: Monet's house and gardens, Giverny
places.summary: The water lilies, the Japanese bridge and Monet's pink house in Normandy.
places.hours_note: Closed in winter: reopens in spring.
places.photo: La Maison vue du Clos Normand.jpg

places.name: Moulin Rouge
places.summary: The red windmill and its cabaret revue, feathers and French cancan included.
places.hours_note: Book ahead.

places.name: Place des Abbesses and its metro
places.summary: The village square of Montmartre, with one of the last glass-roofed Art Nouveau metro entrances by Guimard. Take the spiral stairs down: the station is one of the deepest in Paris.
places.photo: Station Métro Abbesses Ligne 12 - Paris XVIII (FR75) - 2022-06-01 - 5.jpg

places.name: The Wall of I Love Yous
places.summary: “I love you” written 311 times in 250 languages on blue enamel tiles, in a little garden just off the Abbesses square.
places.hours_note: Open with the garden, daytime only

places.name: Bateau-Lavoir
places.summary: Where Picasso painted Les Demoiselles d’Avignon. The studios are private, but the little sloping square with its Wallace fountain is lovely.

places.name: Place du Tertre
places.summary: The painters’ square at the top of the hill, with easels under the trees. Touristy, but a must the first time.

places.name: Montmartre vineyard
places.summary: The last working vineyard of Paris, on the north slope of the hill, facing the Lapin Agile. You see it through the railings.
places.hours_note: Seen from the street; open to visits for the harvest festival in October

places.name: La Maison Rose
places.summary: The little pink house with green shutters painted by Utrillo, at the corner of Rue de l’Abreuvoir. Now a restaurant: lunch on the terrace or just the photo.

places.name: Au Lapin Agile
places.summary: A cabaret in a little house where Picasso and Apollinaire drank. Evenings of old French songs, sung around the tables.

places.name: Allée des Brouillards and Place Dalida
places.summary: A quiet lane of villas with gardens where Renoir lived, ending at the little square with the bust of Dalida.
places.photo: P1260926 Paris XVIII allee des Brouillards rwk.jpg

places.name: The Man who Walked through Walls
places.summary: A man half-stuck in a stone wall: Jean Marais’s statue for Marcel Aymé’s short story. Shake his hand, it is polished by everyone who did.

places.name: Moulin de la Galette
places.summary: One of the two windmills left on the hill, the one Renoir painted at the dance hall below. Walk up Rue Lepic to see it.

places.name: Halle Saint-Pierre
places.summary: An iron market hall at the foot of the Sacré-Cœur, now a museum of naive and outsider art, with a bookshop and a café.
places.photo: Halle Saint Pierre In Montmartre - Paris 2013.jpg

places.name: Montmartre funicular
places.address: Rue Tardieu to Rue du Cardinal-Dubois, 18th
places.summary: A one-minute ride up the hill to the Sacré-Cœur, with a metro ticket. Handy for the way up, nicer to walk down the stairs.

places.name: Montmartre Cemetery
places.summary: A romantic cemetery under a road bridge, with the graves of Dalida, Degas, Stendhal and Truffaut, and many cats.
places.hours_note: Open every day, closes around 5:30 pm in winter

places.name: Parvis de La Défense
places.summary: The big esplanade among the towers of La Défense.

places.name: Avenue des Champs-Élysées
places.summary: The famous avenue, lit up for Christmas.

places.name: Square René-Viviani
places.summary: A small garden facing Notre-Dame, home to the oldest tree in Paris.

places.name: Parvis de la Gare de l'Est
places.summary: The forecourt of the Gare de l'Est.

places.name: Musée Picasso
places.summary: The world's largest Picasso collection, in a grand 17th-century mansion of the Marais.

places.name: Rue des Rosiers
places.summary: The heart of the old Jewish quarter: bakeries, delis and the famous falafel queues.
places.tip: Falafel at L’As du Fallafel, eaten standing in the street.

places.name: Hôtel de Sens
places.summary: One of the last medieval mansions of Paris, with turrets and a formal garden behind.

places.name: Parc de Belleville
places.summary: A park on a slope with one of the best free views over Paris, at the top of the steps.
places.photo: P1010851 Paris XX Parc de Belleville reductwk.JPG

places.name: Rue Dénoyez
places.summary: A short street entirely covered in graffiti, repainted all the time.

places.name: Parc des Buttes-Chaumont
places.summary: Cliffs, a lake and a little temple on a rock: the most romantic park in Paris.

places.name: La Bellevilloise
places.summary: An old workers’ cooperative turned into a bar, club and concert hall, with olive trees under a glass roof.

places.name: Bassin de la Villette
places.summary: The wide basin where the canal opens up: cinemas on both banks, boats, and pétanque along the water.

places.name: Rotonde de la Villette
places.summary: A round toll house by Ledoux from the 1780s, at the end of the canal, now a café.

places.name: Hôtel du Nord
places.summary: The façade of the 1938 Carné film, on the Canal Saint-Martin. Now a bistro.

places.name: Panthéon
places.summary: The great domed temple where France buries its heroes, with Foucault’s pendulum inside.

places.name: Rue Mouffetard
places.summary: A winding medieval street going down the hill, with a morning market at the bottom.
places.tip: Best in the morning, for the market.

places.name: Arènes de Lutèce
places.summary: A Roman amphitheatre hidden behind the buildings, where locals now play pétanque.

places.name: Île Saint-Louis
places.summary: A quiet island of 17th-century houses: walk around the quays and have a Berthillon ice cream.

places.name: Pont Neuf
places.summary: The oldest standing bridge in Paris, with stone benches in its little bays.
places.photo: The western sides of the Île de la Cité and the Pont Neuf, 14 July 2008.jpg

places.name: Flower market
places.summary: Iron pavilions full of plants on the Île de la Cité, open every day.
places.photo: Marché aux fleurs et aux oiseaux de Paris 2010-07-29 n1.jpg

places.name: Café de Flore
places.summary: The café of Sartre and Beauvoir, next to Les Deux Magots. Pricey hot chocolate, perfect people-watching.
places.photo: Café de Flore, 172 boulevard Saint-Germain, Paris 6e.jpg

places.name: Église Saint-Sulpice
places.summary: A huge church with Delacroix murals and a big fountain on its square.

places.name: Rue de la Butte-aux-Cailles
places.summary: A village street of low houses, street art and cheap bars on top of the little hill.
places.photo: Paris 13e - Rue de la Butte-aux-Cailles - vue est 4.jpg

places.name: Butte-aux-Cailles swimming pool
places.summary: A 1920s brick pool under a concrete vault, fed by a natural spring. Bring a swim cap.
places.photo: Piscine de la Butte-aux-Cailles, 5 place Paul-Verlaine, Paris 13e.jpg

places.name: Musée Albert-Kahn and its gardens
places.summary: A banker’s world gardens (Japanese village, English cottage, Vosges forest) and his early colour photographs of the whole planet, just past the edge of Paris.
places.tip: The Japanese garden is lovely in autumn colours.

places.name: Grand Palais
places.summary: The great glass and iron nave of 1900, newly restored. Big exhibitions, and a huge ice rink under the glass roof at Christmas.

places.name: Hammam of the Grande Mosquée
places.summary: Turkish baths under Moorish tiles, then mint tea and pastries in the courtyard of the mosque.
places.hours_note: Women: Mon, Wed, Thu, Sat 10:00–21:00 and Fri 14:00–21:00. Men: Tue 14:00–21:00 and Sun 10:00–21:00. Call before going.
places.tip: Separate entrance, to the left of the pastry shop.

places.name: The old Turkish baths
places.summary: A 19th-century Moorish façade, left from a Turkish bathhouse near the Opéra. Outside only: the building has been converted.

events.title: Renaissance: Da Vinci, Raphael, Michelangelo
events.summary: Da Vinci, Raphael and Michelangelo projected in an immersive show.

events.title: Christmas market at La Défense
events.date_note: Some areas stay open until 3 January.
events.summary: The biggest Christmas market in the Paris region, with hundreds of chalets among the towers.

events.title: Christmas magic at the Tuileries
events.summary: Food chalets, crafts and a funfair in the Tuileries Garden.

events.title: Christmas market on the Champs-Élysées
events.summary: Back after several years, under the avenue's Christmas lights.

events.title: Notre-Dame Christmas market
events.summary: French crafts and artists in the garden facing the cathedral.

events.title: Alsatian Christmas market
events.summary: Alsace specialities and local produce under a heated marquee.

events.title: Montmartre Christmas market
events.summary: Chalets on the Place des Abbesses, at the foot of Montmartre.

events.title: Festival of Lights at the Jardin des Plantes
events.date_note: Mid-November to mid-December, in the evening
events.summary: Giant illuminated sculptures across the botanical garden after dark.

events.title: Beaujolais Nouveau night
events.summary: The new Beaujolais is released on the third Thursday of November: wine bars and bistros celebrate all evening.

events.title: Monet: Painting Time
events.summary: An exhibition around Monet, next to the Water Lilies.

events.title: Auguste Bartholdi: Liberty Enlightening the World
events.summary: The sculptor of the Statue of Liberty, at the Musée d'Orsay.

events.title: The Eternal Tintoretto
events.summary: Venetian painting in the setting of a Parisian mansion.

events.title: Remember Me
events.summary: Contemporary art under the painted dome.

events.title: Belmondo: Le Magnifique (Cinémathèque française)
events.summary: An exhibition on Jean-Paul Belmondo, with screenings.

events.title: Grand Palais des Glaces (ice rink)
events.summary: The biggest indoor ice rink, under the glass roof of the Grand Palais. From about €27 (morning) to €39 (evening).

areas.name: Montmartre
areas.summary: The village on the hill: steep lanes, stairs, windmills, a vineyard and painters' squares. Best done on foot, from the Abbesses up to the Sacré-Cœur, then down the stairs.
areas.best_time: Morning, or late afternoon for the sunset from the Sacré-Cœur

areas.name: Le Marais
areas.summary: Aristocratic mansions turned into museums, tiny streets, falafel and vintage shops, between the Hôtel de Ville and the Place des Vosges.
areas.best_time: Sunday, when the shops are open and the streets busy

areas.name: The islands
areas.summary: Where Paris began: the Île de la Cité with Notre-Dame and the Sainte-Chapelle, and the quiet Île Saint-Louis next door.
areas.best_time: Morning, before the crowds at Notre-Dame

areas.name: Latin Quarter
areas.summary: The students' Paris since the Middle Ages: the Sorbonne, the Panthéon, a Roman arena and the market street of Mouffetard.

areas.name: Saint-Germain-des-Prés
areas.summary: Literary cafés, art galleries, Delacroix's studio and the Luxembourg garden, on the left bank.

areas.name: Louvre & Palais-Royal
areas.summary: The royal heart of the right bank: the Louvre, the Tuileries, the arcades of the Palais-Royal and the first covered passages.
areas.duration: Half a day (a day with the Louvre)

areas.name: Opéra & the covered passages
areas.summary: Glass-roofed 19th-century passages, the Palais Garnier and the department stores of the Grands Boulevards. Perfect when it rains.

areas.name: Canal Saint-Martin
areas.summary: Iron footbridges, locks and plane trees along the canal, up to the wide Bassin de la Villette.
areas.best_time: Sunday, when the quays are closed to cars

areas.name: Belleville & Ménilmontant
areas.summary: The working-class hills of the east: street art, Chinatown, a view over all of Paris and the Père-Lachaise.
areas.best_time: Late afternoon, for the view from the Parc de Belleville

areas.name: Bastille & Bercy
areas.summary: An old railway turned into a garden walk, pastel houses, a Belle Époque station restaurant and fairground museums.

areas.name: Butte-aux-Cailles
areas.summary: A little village of low houses and flowered alleys on a hill of the 13th, with an Art Deco swimming pool.

areas.name: Montparnasse
areas.summary: The artists' quarter of the 1920s, the Catacombs underground and the best view of the Eiffel Tower from the tower.

areas.name: Eiffel Tower & Invalides
areas.summary: The Eiffel Tower, the Champ-de-Mars and the quiet, grand streets of the 7th, with the Rodin garden.

areas.name: Champs-Élysées & Monceau
areas.summary: The grand avenue, the Arc de Triomphe and the private mansions-turned-museums around the Parc Monceau.
areas.best_time: Sunset at the Arc de Triomphe

areas.name: Passy
areas.summary: The quiet, wealthy west: Art Nouveau buildings, Monet's water lilies and a cobbled lane where Balzac lived.

areas.name: Around Paris
areas.summary: Day trips by train: castles, gardens and the flea market just outside the city.
